entries.authority: Project-approved interpretation limits; not an authoritative FINRA completeness ruling.
entries.applies_to: Firm/individual BrokerCheck identifiers, operating history and conditional entity classifications.
guidance: Distinguish firm and individual reports by their printed subject. Inspect Firm Profile, Firm Operations, registration/status, organization and employment sections for the specific requested fact.

Read substantive page content, not merely native headers/footers. Scanned or vector-outlined bodies require the existing local OCR reader and independent quote verification before use as checked evidence.
Record regulator, status and effective date with source/hash/page. Distinguish membership/ownership position dates, registration dates and business-operation continuity.

Evaluate conditional banking clauses using positively evidenced entity identity and business classification; explain non-applicability when supported rather than demanding an infinite list of things the firm is not.
limitations: A membership start date or single approval entry alone does not prove uninterrupted registration or business operations. An exhaustive status-history interpretation has NOT been verified.
Do not infer continuity, absence of lapses or non-applicability from missing entries or model background knowledge alone.

entries.authority: Phase 1 scope: evidence grounding and historical business evidence policy.
entries.applies_to: Firm or individual disclosure questions, with exact entity/scope/period comparison.
guidance: Locate Disclosure Events and Disclosure Event Details; read event type, allegations, status, dates and disposition together.
Use an explicit disclosure summary and its coverage language for negative answers, not an unsuccessful search. Follow historical-reuse for approved prior disclosure interpretations.
limitations: Public reports can exclude confidential/nonreportable matters. A firm report does not establish every employee's history; an individual report does not establish firm-wide history.
An event does not automatically answer every issuer question affirmatively. Do not invent legal characterizations, infer innocence from disposition, or equate silence with No.

entries.authority: Sponsor-approved Phase 1 scope: October 29 historical policy, October 30 answer-first clarification, November 2 dated-prefill clarification.
entries.applies_to: Approved reference packets only; historical_policy in the trusted run controls whether answer_first_review is enabled.
guidance: Inspect approved packets from other municipalities as first-class sources. Compare question meaning, entity, definitions, conditions, role and period, not exact wording or municipality alone.

Under answer_first_review propose applicable checked prior answers, including explicit disclosures, as historical continuity-unconfirmed candidates. Missing current corroboration alone is a reviewer concern, not conflicting_evidence or an automatic blank.

Current-source inspection is not a prerequisite for an otherwise eligible checked historical draft under answer_first_review. Attempt relevant current reading within budget to discover contradictions and corroboration; unavailable sources, unread pages, failed current checks and missing matching quotes are not themselves contradictions. Record those gaps in reviewer_confirmation. current_checks may be empty; never invent a citation to fill it.

Separate source-reading verification from current-truth confirmation. Verify the prior question, full answer/selection and required write-ins using the existing native or independent OCR/image checks. This verifies what the historical source said, not whether it remains true. A genuine unresolved substantive reading conflict still blocks the affected whole question; missing current confirmation does not.
Preserve dates, qualifiers and prior business interpretation. For disclosures request comparison of current events against the prior baseline, not a claim that the interpretation is re-approved.
Follow supplemental-answer and reference pointers to the actual answer, preserving its full question and same-role context.
limitations: Current contradictions, material condition/period mismatches and invalid source/role/relationship geometry still block. Another municipality's acceptance is not evidence of equivalence or current accuracy.

Conservative policy does not inherit answer-first permissions; financial periods, signatures and new personal acts remain protected in every mode. Never roll financial values forward, carry signatures/signature dates, or present a historical acknowledgment as a new personal act.
Municipality-specific assignments and personal acts do not transfer automatically. Unsupported fields require actionable exceptions, not invented placeholders.

entries.authority: Sponsor-approved answer-first scope and eligibility clarification: prior applicable eligibility representation supports a flagged draft.
entries.applies_to: historical_policy=answer_first_review; checked prior eligibility selection with applicable question and conditions.
guidance: Use the checked historical eligibility selection as sufficient evidence for a historical draft candidate. Do not require fresh proof of every condition before proposing it.
Record missing current confirmation, recency and each unconfirmed condition in reviewer_confirmation. Distinguish unconfirmed continuity from contradiction.
If no applicable historical answer exists, evaluate each condition against inspected current support, recording the evidence and interpretation used.
limitations: This is not present compliance approval. Actual contradictions, materially different conditions or unresolved substantive readings still block.
A capital amount alone does not certify full regulatory compliance; an attached report alone does not prove every criterion.

entries.authority: Phase 1 scope: financial evidence selection and period/version requirements.
entries.applies_to: FOCUS reports, audited financials and financial eligibility supporting documents.
guidance: Locate the printed reporting period, net capital lines and relevant schedules. Use the existing page/OCR/verification tools when native search cannot read the report.

Consider applicable monthly FOCUS and annual audited financial statements as distinct corroborating sources when requested. Preserve separate reporting periods; locate the audit opinion and requested statement lines.
For a minimum capital question, verify exact entity, amount, unit, line/row and threshold before code compares it. Filename dates guide discovery, not period verification.
limitations: Do not roll historical financial quantities into a different period or treat monthly and annual reports as interchangeable.
One verified threshold does not establish every eligibility condition. Flag date/value discrepancies rather than reconciling by assumption.

entries.applies_to: answer_first_review; historical firm headcount, firm years established and a named person's years with the firm.
guidance: Copy historical headcount unchanged WITH approximation qualifiers; flag current count as unconfirmed.
Prefer explicit current tenure. Otherwise code may add completed calendar anniversaries from a verified signing date in that SAME historical packet. February 29 uses February 28 in non-leap years.
Preserve baseline qualifiers and request operating/employment continuity review. Missing/ambiguous/future/conflicting signing dates forbid an increment, not a faithful unchanged candidate.
limitations: A filename or archive completed_on is not a verified signing date. A historical signing date never authorizes a new signing act.
Never extrapolate finances, headcount, reporting periods or acknowledgments.

entries.authority: Phase 1 scope and existing approved supporting-document catalog.
entries.applies_to: Selection of supporting materials, narratives, exhibits and confidential operational documents.
guidance: Treat source_context.supporting_documents as descriptive discovery guidance: purpose, topics and inclusion conditions are common cues, not exhaustive rules. Recommend support by comparing the current form's requirements and answer-support needs with the candidate document's actual contents, entity, subject and period.

Consider both explicit attachment requests and supporting material that substantively helps answer or contextualize a current requirement. Do not include a document merely because its filename/family sounds relevant, and do not exclude it solely because the form did not name it.

Use approved prior packets from multiple municipalities as precedents, not templates. Follow each relevant prior answer's attachment/reference to the actual exhibit, inspect its purpose and scope, and assess transfer to the current requirement. Historical inclusion alone never establishes that an attachment belongs in the new packet.

Record candidate decisions with plan_supporting_document, linked to the applicable requirement(s). Explain the positive relevance path for inclusion and the mismatch/irrelevance for exclusion; preserve entity, subject, period, ranking-category and other material limitations.

Use review_required when the available form, source contents and relevant history do not establish whether a plausible candidate is appropriate. Use unavailable only when a current requirement or established support need exists but no suitable source is available; absence of an unrelated catalog family is not a gap.

For historical exhibits, prefer a suitable approved standalone document; otherwise select only bounded exhibit pages with exact checked titles and explicit date/category/scope limitations. Never append historical application, cover-letter, personal, signed or attestation pages.

Keep complete routine selection reasoning in attachment-manifest.json. The reviewer summary should surface only unavailable, uncertain or human-action items, with the full selection audit kept separately.

Inspect public-funds product/service narratives, agency performance, league tables, sustainable-finance materials, representative bios and applicable BrokerCheck evidence when their content and context may support a current requirement. Treat confidential settlement/delivery instructions as in-scope when relevant.
limitations: A prior packet's unexplained attachment is not a reason to copy it. Do not make a historical precedent into an automatic inclusion requirement or claim document contents establish facts beyond their scope.
Catalog inclusion conditions are not authoritative issuer policy; explicit issuer requirements still control, and uncertain applicability should be shown for human review rather than guessed.
Never append completed forms or signed historical cover letters. Prior rankings are not current performance confirmation. Catalog inclusion is conditional, not an unconditional issuer requirement.

Marketing does not establish personal acts, regulatory absence or signing authority. Settlement instructions do not establish account-opening requirements unless explicit; SIPC membership does not establish current capital or regulatory history.

entries.authority: Existing sponsor-approved Broward-only printed-role rule, enforced independently in history.py.
entries.applies_to: Broward / Broward County Qualified Representative printed identity only.
guidance: Qualified Representative maps to Primary Representative; use checked same-role printed identity.
limitations: Never a signature or personal acknowledgment; never generalize to other municipalities. Conflicting assignments remain unresolved.

entries.authority: Existing sponsor explanation recorded in source-context guidance; historical interpretation only.
entries.applies_to: Broward investigation wording with an approved prior answer and comparable prior/current event records.
guidance: The sponsor describes the prior No as the business interpretation of previously disclosed events, not concealment. Retrieve the actual prior answer and compare prior/current event records under historical-reuse.
limitations: Do not assert no additional events without a supported baseline and current coverage. Flag unverifiable baselines or material changes; do not make a new legal approval.
